newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets restructuring of satellite body Inmarsat.
newsitem.headline: EU vets restructuring of satellite body Inmarsat.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it was reviewing a proposal to transform international satellite communications organisation Inmarsat into a commercial company.

It said Inmarsat, which is currently a cooperative based in London of telecommunication companies in about 80 countries, submitted the draft agreement for clearance under EU rules which ban restrictive practices and abuse of dominant positions on March 17.

Inmarsat provides communications for ships, aircrafts, trucks and trains. It is also sponsoring together with a number of European telecoms operators global personal mobile communications systems in Inmarsat-P.

The organisation is the sole provider of satellite services which support the International Maritime Organisation's global maritime distress and safety system (GMDSS), the Commission said in a notice published in the European Union's Official Journal.

It said the new company would conduct all Inmarsat's future and existing business. A residual intergovernmental organisation would remain to oversee and enforce the company's GMDSS services and its other public service obligations.
The relationship between Inmarsat and its partners, who are currently represented in the organisation's council, would also become more "arm's length and contractual", the Commission said.
It gave interested third parties 10 days to comment on the proposed agreement. There is deadline for it to take a final decision.

In December 1996, the Commission dropped an investigation into Iridium, a Motorola-led mobile satellite system rival to Inmarsat-P, saying it had found no grounds for action under EU fair competition rules.
